items.prompt:
Straight-down orthographic plan photograph of a built live-action film set: camera axis exactly perpendicular to the ground; no wall face, no elevation, no side of any building or tree trunk is visible; only the ground plane, the top edges of walls, the tops of roofs, furniture and tree crowns are seen. The top of the image is north. A large low Victorian below-stairs kitchen with its ceiling removed. A long rectangle filling most of the image, enclosed by continuous thick limewashed brick wall lines on all four sides; outside the walls is plain dark. Floor: worn uneven grey stone flags dusted with grey-brown pepper, broken crockery and a frying-pan lying about. Left (west) end wall: at its middle a wide deep open hearth recess in the wall thickness with glowing embers and a round black iron cauldron seen from above on an iron crane, framed by a band of sooted pastel whiplash-vine tiles; in front of it a raised flagstone hearth slab with a rag hearth rug. Exact centre of the floor: a small round three-legged wooden stool standing alone. Top (north) wall: a long scrubbed pale deal table against the wall left of centre with a large pepper-box and open pepper sacks; right of it a tall painted dresser against the wall seen as a long narrow top with racks of blue-and-white plates, shattered plates on the floor below it. Right (east) end wall: a rail of dull copper saucepans against the wall. Bottom (south) wall: fully present along the bottom edge, seen only as its top edge; in its middle a door-width gap with the plank door leaf swung inward against the wall, flanked by two narrow window gaps; a pot of scarlet geraniums on one sill. A light haze of grey-brown pepper smoke that does not hide the floor, thickest over the hearth; warm orange firelight from the hearth fading across the flags, a cool pale daylight patch at the door gap. Door panels, the bell-board and anything mounted on a wall face are not visible from directly above and must not be drawn. Clean base image for a layout plan: no people, no animals, no birds, no creatures, no text, no labels, no arrows, no grid lines, no compass.
 Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
